goal: Implement a locally consented, resumable verified-setup workflow in the Android app while preserving every Android and Kodi confirmation and reporting completion only from observed Bootstrap state.
success_criteria: A second TV-local consent screen has Cancel focused first, accurately lists automated and manual steps, and exposes a Stop automated setup action while a run is live.

Consent is one-run, schema-versioned, scope-bound, expires within 24 hours, survives process restart safely, and is invalidated by cancellation, revocation, expiry, completion, clock rollback, app/config scope change, or stale callbacks.
Every remote mutating command requests local consent and performs zero download, install, export, profile-write, or launch side effects before local grant.
The strict flow never invokes KodiProfileConfigurator and never bypasses Android PackageInstaller, Kodi Unknown Sources, ZIP selection, or Bootstrap approval.

PackageInstaller explicitly requires user action where supported; preparation/export is idempotent; denial or failure pauses without prompt loops; Android waits for observed Bootstrap applied-version evidence rather than a user assertion.
Focused Android tests cover consent, command gating, expiry/revocation, resume, stale callbacks, visible confirmations, no duplicate commits, and the strict no-profile-writer boundary.
primary_hypothesis: A typed, scope-bound local consent state machine can safely automate verified preparation and resume around platform confirmations without expanding the command or installation trust boundaries.
discriminating_check: Exercise every remote mutating entry point before and after local consent and prove that all side effects are blocked before grant while required Android and Kodi confirmations remain visible.
stop_conditions: A required behavior needs silent install, ADB, shell, accessibility, root, database edits, arbitrary paths or commands, or remote consent.
Implementation requires a secret, external mutation, or expansion of the existing trust boundary.
The existing architecture cannot observe Bootstrap applied-version without adding a new external service or broad telemetry surface.
